Pathology + সূচক ও লগারিদম.question: ১) Bacterial spores are destroyed by following process excludes...?
Pathology + সূচক ও লগারিদম.exp:
Bacterial spores are highly resistant to heat and many disinfectants. Boiling at 100°C does not reliably destroy bacterial spores, so it is not considered a sterilization method.

The following methods can destroy bacterial spores:

  • Autoclaving: Moist heat under pressure; highly effective for spore destruction.

  • Hot air oven: Dry heat sterilization; destroys spores with adequate temperature and exposure time.

  • Gamma radiation: Ionizing radiation capable of destroying bacterial spores.

Why boiling is incorrect:
Boiling kills many vegetative bacteria, but spores can survive ordinary boiling.

High-yield Sterilization recall:
Autoclave: 121°C, 15 psi, ~15 minutes is the classic exam standard for sterilization.

Exam pearl:
Boiling ≠ reliable sterilization because bacterial spores may survive.

Pathology + সূচক ও লগারিদম.question: ২) Sharp cutting instruments are sterilized by which method?
Pathology + সূচক ও লগারিদম.exp:
Sharp cutting instruments such as scalpels and some cutting tools may be damaged or lose their sharpness with repeated moist heat sterilization. In older/classical exam questions, chemical methods such as Lysol may be cited for instruments that cannot tolerate heat.

However, Lysol is a disinfectant, not a reliable sterilizing agent, and modern practice generally uses appropriate validated sterilization methods for surgical instruments.

Why the other options are less appropriate:

  • Autoclave: Effective sterilization method, but repeated exposure may affect some sharp instruments; however, many modern surgical instruments are routinely autoclaved.

  • Boiling: Does not reliably destroy bacterial spores, so it is not sterilization.

  • Formaldehyde: Can be used as a chemical sterilant under appropriate conditions, but is not the classic answer for sharp cutting instruments in this MCQ.

High-yield Sterilization recall:
Autoclave → moist heat sterilization; Hot-air oven → dry heat, useful for glassware and metal instruments.

Exam pearl:
For this classical MCQ, choose Lysol, but remember: Lysol is a disinfectant, not a dependable modern sterilizing method.

Pathology + সূচক ও লগারিদম.question: ৩) Mechanism of action of moist heat is..?
Pathology + সূচক ও লগারিদম.option1: loss of functional integrity of cytoplasmic membrane
Pathology + সূচক ও লগারিদম.exp:
The primary mechanism of moist heat (e.g., autoclaving) is denaturation and coagulation of cellular proteins. Moist heat is more effective than dry heat because water facilitates protein denaturation at lower temperatures.

  • Autoclave: 121°C, 15 psi, typically 15 minutes

  • Main effect → protein denaturation

Why the other options are incorrect:

  • Loss of functional integrity of cytoplasmic membrane: Can occur with heat, but it is not the primary mechanism of moist-heat sterilization.

  • Oxidative damage: More characteristic of dry heat sterilization.

  • All: Incorrect because the classic mechanism is protein denaturation.

High-yield Sterilization recall:
Moist heat → protein denaturation
Dry heat → oxidative damage

Exam pearl:
Moist heat kills microorganisms mainly by denaturing proteins.

Pathology + সূচক ও লগারিদম.question: ৪) Which one is correct regarding autoclaving process of sterilization?
Pathology + সূচক ও লগারিদম.exp:
Autoclaving is a moist heat sterilization method using saturated steam under pressure. The classic standard is:

  • Temperature: 121°C

  • Pressure: 15 psi (approximately 1 bar above atmospheric pressure)

  • Time: 15 minutes

This combination reliably destroys vegetative bacteria, viruses, fungi, and bacterial spores.

Why the other options are incorrect:

  • 100°C for 60 minutes: Boiling temperature; does not reliably destroy spores.

  • 100°C for 15 minutes: Equivalent to boiling, not sterilization.

  • 121°C for 60 minutes: Excessive exposure; not the standard cycle.

High-yield Sterilization recall:
Autoclave = 121°C + 15 psi + 15 minutes.

Exam pearl:
Remember “121–15–15” for the classic autoclave MCQ.

Pathology + সূচক ও লগারিদম.question: ৫) In HTST method of pasteurization heating is done at....?
Pathology + সূচক ও লগারিদম.exp:
HTST (High-Temperature Short-Time) pasteurization heats milk to 72°C for 15 seconds. This effectively destroys important pathogenic organisms while preserving the quality of milk.

Why the other options are incorrect:

  • 63°C for 30 minutes: This is the Holder/LTLT method.

  • 132°C for 5 seconds: Not the standard HTST method.

  • 133°C for 1–2 seconds: More consistent with UHT-type processing, not HTST.

Exam pearl:
HTST = 72°C for 15 seconds.

Pathology + সূচক ও লগারিদম.question: ৬) For the preservation of fresh tissue which formaldehyde preparation is used?
Pathology + সূচক ও লগারিদম.exp:
For preservation/fixation of fresh tissue, the standard preparation used is 10% formalin (preferably 10% neutral buffered formalin).

Important distinction:

  • Commercial formaldehyde solution is approximately 37–40%.

  • Diluting this to 10% formalin gives approximately 4% formaldehyde, which is the routine tissue fixative.

Why the other options are incorrect:

  • 30%: Too concentrated for routine tissue fixation.

  • 40%: Commercial concentrated formaldehyde stock; not used directly for routine tissue preservation.

  • 90–99%: Not appropriate as a tissue fixative.

High-yield Histopathology recall:
10% formalin ≈ 4% formaldehyde and is the routine fixative for histopathological specimens.

Exam pearl:
Fresh tissue preservation → 10% formalin (≈4% formaldehyde).

Pathology + সূচক ও লগারিদম.question: ৭) The process of destruction of all vegetative forms of pathogenic organism from living surface is called..?
Pathology + সূচক ও লগারিদম.exp:
Antisepsis is the process of destroying or inhibiting vegetative forms of pathogenic microorganisms on living tissues/surfaces using antiseptic agents.

Why the other options are incorrect:

  • Sterilization: Destruction/removal of all forms of microbial life, including spores; generally applies to inanimate objects.

  • Disinfection: Destruction of pathogenic microorganisms on inanimate objects, usually not bacterial spores.

  • Decontamination: Removal or reduction of contaminants to make an object or surface safe to handle; broader term.

High-yield Microbiology recall:
Living tissue → Antisepsis
Inanimate surface → Disinfection
All microorganisms including spores → Sterilization

Exam pearl:
Antisepsis = destruction/inhibition of pathogens on living tissue.

Pathology + সূচক ও লগারিদম.question: ৮) Features of gastrointestinal mucosal toxicity due to radiation exposure excludes..?
Pathology + সূচক ও লগারিদম.exp:
Gastrointestinal mucosal toxicity from radiation exposure causes severe injury to rapidly dividing intestinal mucosal cells. Typical features include profuse diarrhoea, vomiting, abdominal pain, dehydration, and sepsis due to mucosal barrier breakdown and bacterial translocation.

GIT bleeding is not a typical primary feature of gastrointestinal radiation toxicity, so it is the best answer for the exception.

Why the other options are features:

  • Profound diarrhoea: Due to severe intestinal mucosal damage.

  • Vomiting: Common in significant radiation exposure.

  • Sepsis: Results from disruption of the intestinal barrier and bacterial translocation.

High-yield Radiation injury recall:
GI radiation syndrome → vomiting + severe diarrhoea + mucosal injury + bacterial translocation → sepsis.

Exam pearl:
Radiation GI toxicity classically causes severe vomiting and diarrhoea with risk of sepsis.

Pathology + সূচক ও লগারিদম.question: ৯) Management of a large dose radiation exposure should be following -
Pathology + সূচক ও লগারিদম.exp:
Management of large-dose radiation exposure is mainly supportive and multidisciplinary. Important measures include:

  • Adequate hydration → correct fluid and electrolyte disturbances.

  • Control of sepsis/infection → radiation-induced mucosal injury and neutropenia increase the risk of infection.

  • Management of bone marrow aplasia → may require hematopoietic growth factors, blood products, and in selected severe cases hematopoietic stem-cell transplantation.

Therefore, all of the above are appropriate components of management.

High-yield Radiation injury recall:
Major acute radiation syndrome management = supportive care + infection control + treatment of hematopoietic failure + management of GI complications.

Exam pearl:
Large radiation exposure → hydrate + control infection/sepsis + manage marrow aplasia.

Pathology + সূচক ও লগারিদম.question: ১০) Which is the sterilization procedure for culture media containing sugar?
Pathology + সূচক ও লগারিদম.exp:
Culture media containing sugar are preferably sterilized by tyndallization (fractional sterilization) because prolonged heating at high temperature may decompose or caramelize sugars and alter the medium.

Tyndallization involves intermittent steaming at about 100°C for ~20–30 minutes on 3 successive days. The first heating kills vegetative bacteria; spores germinate during incubation and are then destroyed by subsequent heating.

Why the other options are less appropriate:

  • Autoclave: High temperature may cause sugar degradation/caramelization in sugar-containing media.

  • Steaming: A single steaming cycle may not reliably destroy spores.

  • Hot air oven: Dry heat is unsuitable for most culture media.

High-yield Sterilization recall:
Sugar-containing culture media → Tyndallization (fractional sterilization).

Exam pearl:
Sugar-containing media → Tyndallization, because autoclaving may caramelize/decompose sugars.

Pathology + সূচক ও লগারিদম.question: ১১) Unprotected miners of radioactive elements have a 10 fold increased risk of..... cancer?
Pathology + সূচক ও লগারিদম.exp:
Unprotected miners working with radioactive elements, particularly uranium miners, have a markedly increased risk of lung cancer. The major mechanism involves exposure to radon and its radioactive decay products, which can cause chronic alpha-particle irradiation of the respiratory epithelium.

Why the other options are incorrect:

  • Stomach: Not the characteristic occupational cancer in radioactive-element miners.

  • Bladder: Associated more classically with certain chemical occupational exposures.

  • Genital: Not the characteristic cancer associated with uranium/radon mining.

High-yield Occupational cancer recall:
Uranium/radon miners → Lung cancer.
Radon → alpha radiation → bronchogenic carcinoma.

Exam pearl:
Unprotected uranium miners have a markedly increased risk of lung cancer due to radon exposure.

Pathology + সূচক ও লগারিদম.question: ১২) Filtration is suitable method for sterilization of.....?
Pathology + সূচক ও লগারিদম.exp:
Filtration is used for sterilizing heat-sensitive liquids that cannot tolerate autoclaving. IV fluids, such as certain heat-labile solutions, can be sterilized by passing them through a membrane filter that physically removes microorganisms.

Why the other options are incorrect:

  • Surgical gauzes: Usually sterilized by autoclaving.

  • Culture media: Usually sterilized by autoclaving; special heat-sensitive media may require alternative methods.

  • Catheter: Usually sterilized by appropriate heat or chemical/gas sterilization depending on material.

High-yield Sterilization recall:
Filtration → heat-sensitive liquids and gases.
Examples: IV fluids, serum, antibiotic solutions, enzyme solutions.

Exam pearl:
Heat-sensitive IV fluid → membrane filtration for sterilization.

Pathology + সূচক ও লগারিদম.question: ১৩) All of the followings occurs due to exposure to UV except.....?
Pathology + সূচক ও লগারিদম.exp:
Chronic exposure to UV radiation, particularly UV-B, is strongly associated with cutaneous malignancies, including:

  • BCC (Basal cell carcinoma)

  • SCC (Squamous cell carcinoma)

  • Malignant melanoma (MM)

Non-Hodgkin lymphoma (NHL) is not a typical cancer caused by UV radiation.

Why the other options are associated:

  • BCC: Strong association with cumulative UV exposure.

  • SCC: Strong association with chronic UV exposure.

  • Malignant melanoma: UV exposure is an important environmental risk factor.

High-yield Radiation recall:
UV radiation → BCC + SCC + melanoma.

Exam pearl:
UV exposure causes skin cancers, not NHL.

Pathology + সূচক ও লগারিদম.question: ১৪) Which one is sterilization procedure for catheter?
Pathology + সূচক ও লগারিদম.exp:
Catheters, especially disposable plastic catheters, are commonly sterilized industrially using gamma radiation. Gamma rays provide effective sterilization without requiring high temperatures, making them suitable for heat-sensitive plastic medical devices.

Why the other options are less appropriate:

  • Autoclave: Uses high-temperature moist heat; may deform or damage many plastic catheters.

  • Hot air oven: Requires high dry heat and is unsuitable for most plastic catheters.

  • Steaming: Not an appropriate standard sterilization method for heat-sensitive disposable catheters.

High-yield Sterilization recall:
Gamma radiation → disposable plastic medical devices such as catheters, syringes, and surgical gloves.

Exam pearl:
Heat-sensitive disposable catheter → Gamma radiation.

Pathology + সূচক ও লগারিদম.question: ১৫) Which one is used as protection against beta particles?
Pathology + সূচক ও লগারিদম.exp:
Beta particles are relatively light, high-energy electrons or positrons. They are best shielded using low-atomic-number materials, particularly aluminium or plastic.

  • Paper → adequate for alpha particles

  • Aluminium → suitable for beta particles

  • Lead → mainly used for gamma/X-rays, but high-Z materials can produce secondary bremsstrahlung with beta radiation

  • Concrete → mainly used for gamma/neutron shielding

High-yield Radiation protection recall:

Radiation Typical shielding
Alpha (α) Paper / skin
Beta (β) Aluminium / plastic
Gamma (γ) Lead / concrete
Neutron Water / concrete

Exam pearl:
Beta radiation → Aluminium shielding.

Pathology + সূচক ও লগারিদম.question: ১৬) Which one is most effective antiseptic?
Pathology + সূচক ও লগারিদম.exp:
Iodine is a highly effective broad-spectrum antiseptic. It rapidly acts against Gram-positive and Gram-negative bacteria, fungi, viruses, and some spores. Povidone-iodine is commonly used as a skin antiseptic.

Why the other options are less appropriate:

  • Alcohol: Excellent rapid-acting antiseptic, but less effective against bacterial spores and some non-enveloped viruses.

  • Cetrimide: A quaternary ammonium compound with mainly antibacterial activity; less broad-spectrum than iodine.

  • Cresol: A phenolic disinfectant, primarily used for environmental/inanimate surfaces rather than routine skin antisepsis.

High-yield Antiseptic recall:
Iodine → broad-spectrum antiseptic; alcohol → rapid action but no reliable sporicidal activity.

Exam pearl:
Among the given options, iodine is the most effective broad-spectrum antiseptic.

Pathology + সূচক ও লগারিদম.question: ১৭) Which is a non ionizing radiation?
Pathology + সূচক ও লগারিদম.exp:
Laser radiation is a form of non-ionizing electromagnetic radiation. Its photons do not have sufficient energy to ionize atoms under ordinary conditions.

  • Gamma rays: Ionizing electromagnetic radiation

  • X-rays: Ionizing electromagnetic radiation

  • Neutrons: Ionizing radiation because they can produce secondary ionizing interactions

High-yield Radiation recall:
Ionizing: X-rays, gamma rays, alpha particles, beta particles, neutrons.
Non-ionizing: Radio waves, microwaves, infrared, visible light, lasers, and most UV.

Exam pearl:
Laser = non-ionizing radiation.

Pathology + সূচক ও লগারিদম.question: ১৮) All of the tissues are particularly sensitive to ionizing radiation except.......?
Pathology + সূচক ও লগারিদম.exp:
The sensitivity of tissues to ionizing radiation depends largely on their rate of cell division and degree of differentiation.

Highly radiosensitive tissues include:

  • Bone marrow → rapidly dividing hematopoietic cells

  • Gonads → especially spermatogonia

  • Lymphoid tissue → highly sensitive

The thyroid is comparatively less radiosensitive than these tissues, although it is clinically important because radioactive iodine can accumulate in the thyroid and increase the risk of thyroid cancer, especially after childhood exposure.

Why the other options are incorrect:

  • Bone marrow: Highly radiosensitive.

  • Gonads: Highly radiosensitive, particularly germinal epithelium.

  • Skin: Relatively radiosensitive and develops erythema, epilation, etc., after sufficient exposure.

High-yield Radiation recall:
Most radiosensitive: lymphoid tissue → bone marrow → gonads → intestinal epithelium.

Exam pearl:
Thyroid is comparatively less radiosensitive than bone marrow and gonads.

Pathology + সূচক ও লগারিদম.question: ১৯) Hexisol contains....?
Pathology + সূচক ও লগারিদম.exp:
Hexisol is a commonly used alcohol-based hand antiseptic containing chlorhexidine along with alcohol. Chlorhexidine provides persistent antimicrobial activity, while alcohol provides rapid antimicrobial action.

Why the other options are incorrect:

  • Chlorhexidine only: Incomplete; Hexisol also contains alcohol.

  • Alcohol only: Incomplete; chlorhexidine is also present.

  • None: Incorrect.

High-yield Antiseptic recall:
Chlorhexidine + alcohol is an effective combination for rapid and persistent hand antisepsis.

Exam pearl:
Hexisol = Chlorhexidine + Alcohol.

Pathology + সূচক ও লগারিদম.question: ২০) Which is an acute effect of radiation exposure?
Pathology + সূচক ও লগারিদম.exp:
Sepsis can occur as an acute effect of high-dose radiation exposure, particularly in acute radiation syndrome with severe bone marrow suppression and gastrointestinal mucosal injury. Neutropenia and breakdown of the intestinal barrier predispose to serious infections and sepsis.

The other options are mainly late effects:

  • Infertility: A delayed tissue effect, especially after gonadal irradiation.

  • Cataract: Late radiation effect, particularly after significant lens exposure.

  • Neoplasia: Late stochastic effect of radiation.

High-yield Radiation recall:
Acute effects: nausea, vomiting, diarrhoea, bone marrow suppression, infection/sepsis.
Late effects: cataract, infertility, fibrosis, malignancy.

Exam pearl:
High-dose radiation → acute marrow/GI injury → infection and sepsis.
